tagline: A quantum circuit laboratory in your browser
lead: Two qubits and two gates are enough to show the two ideas everything else rests on. The circuit below is not a picture of one: it runs in this tab, a stage at a time.

cta.note: The editor opens with six worked circuits beside it, ready to run and to take apart.

demo.heading: Two gates: superposition and entanglement
demo.intro: Each stage is a circuit that runs when it is shown. The chart lists every outcome the pair can give, and how often.

chart.heading: Outcomes, and how often
chart.caption: Every reading the two wires can give. A bar with no length is an outcome that never happens.

zero.name: Nothing yet
zero.circuit: Two qubits, {{q0}} and {{q1}}, with no gate on either.
zero.story: Measure them now and both give 0, every time. One outcome, one bar, nothing else on the chart. An ordinary pair of bits would stay here.

superposed.name: One gate
superposed.circuit: {{h}} on {{q0}} — the gate that puts a qubit into superposition.
superposed.story: One bar became two. {{q0}} gives 0 half the time and 1 half the time, and this is not a coin whose value you simply do not know yet: both outcomes are really there, and the next gate acts on both at once. That is superposition.

independent.name: Two coins
independent.story: Four bars, a quarter each. Both qubits are in superposition and neither says anything about the other: learning that {{q0}} gave 1 leaves {{q1}} exactly as undecided as before. Two independent coins.

entangled.name: One pair
entangled.circuit: {{h}} on {{q0}}, then {{cnot}}: it flips {{q1}} whenever {{q0}} reads 1.
entangled.story: Each qubit still reads 1 half the time — the two figures below have not moved. But two of the four outcomes are gone, and the pair now always agrees. Neither qubit has an answer of its own any more; only the pair does. That is entanglement.

notation.before: Each bar is one reading of the two wires, written
notation.after: — the lower wire on the left, the top wire on the right.

local.title: In this tab
local.body: The simulation runs in your browser, on a background thread. There is no account, and nothing you build is uploaded anywhere.

link.title: A link is the save file
link.body: The whole circuit travels inside the address. Copy it, send it, and whoever opens it sees exactly what you drew.

state.title: The state, not only the answer
state.body: Amplitude, phase and probability for every basis state, recomputed while you edit, with a timeline that walks the circuit one column at a time.

closing: Everything above is a few dragged gates away in the editor.
